examples.text: We have not been covetous, honourable fathers, to change, neither is it now any new lust that alters our affection, or old lothing, but those needful jealousies of state, that warn wiser princes hourly to provide their safety, and do teach them how learned a thing it is to beware of the humblest enemy; much more of those great ones, whom their own employed favours have made fit for their fears.

I choose rather to live graved in obscurity, than share with them in so preposterous a fame. Nor can I blame the wishes of those severe and wise patriots, who providing the hurts these licentious spirits may do in a state, desire rather to see fools and devils, and those antique relics of barbarism retrieved, with all other ridiculous and exploded follies, than behold the wounds of private men, of princes and nations

glosses: A sleeveless garment that buttons down the front, worn over a shirt, and often as part of a suit; a waistcoat.

examples.text: The Jones man was looking at her hard. Now he reached into the hatch of his vest and fetched out a couple of cigars, everlasting big ones, with gilt bands on them.

glosses: A sleeveless garment, often with a low-cut neck, usually worn under a shirt or blouse.

examples.text: Not seldom, clad in radiant vest / Deceitfully goes forth the morn.

glosses: A loose robe or outer garment worn historically by men in Arab or Middle Eastern countries.
To clothe with, or as with, a vestment, or garment; to dress; to robe; to cover, surround, or encompass closely.

examples.text: Came vested all in white, pure as her mind.
With ether vested, and a purple sky.

glosses: To clothe with authority, power, etc.; to put in possession; to invest; to furnish; to endow; followed by with and the thing conferred.

examples.text: to vest a court with power to try cases of life and death

glosses: To place or give into the possession or discretion of some person or authority; to commit to another; with in before the possessor.

examples.text: The power of life and death is vested in the king, or in the courts.

glosses: To clothe with possession; also, to give a person an immediate fixed right of present or future enjoyment of.

glosses: (of an inheritance or a trust fund) To devolve upon the person currently entitled when a prior interest has ended.

examples.text: Upon the death of the Sovereign the Crown automatically vests in the next heir without the need of coronation or other formality.

glosses: To become vested, to become permanent.

examples.text: My pension vests at the end of the month and then I can take it with me when I quit.
